findings.minimalFix: Check ownership/current unlock eligibility inside the purchase transaction and prevent a closing/pending handler from buying again. Recheck ownership in rewarded-ad completion too. Don't count an already-owned talent as a new unlock.
findings.tests: Two queued paid calls and paid/ad completion race: one debit, one unlock, one TalentUp; failed purchase remains retryable.

findings.title: Loading a battle reapplies one-shot buff rewards and wipes later-earned silver
findings.trigger: Resume any saved battle that includes Buff10, Buff29, or Buff24. loadGame restores saved coin, then calls normal addGameBuff for every saved buff.
findings.evidence: Actual loadGame/setRound/addGameBuff: saved coin77 restores as89 with Buff10 (+12),83 with Buff29 (+6),0 with Buff24. Silver achievement increments again for10/29. Buff11/12/24 building upgrade effects also execute before saved building restoration, but additional damage from those building effects was not asserted.
findings.minimalFix: Separate restoring persistent buff modifiers/list entries from acquiring a buff's one-shot rewards/upgrade effects. On load rebuild persistent modifiers only; preserve exact saved coin, building levels and achievement counters.
findings.tests: Repeat save/load for buffs10/29/24 and building-upgrade11/12; coin/builds/counters unchanged; ongoing stat modifiers restored once. Gameplay agent already owns surrounding combat logic.

findings.title: A battle checkpoint can combine a new round with old business/task state
findings.trigger: Interruption after setBuildInfoList saves new round/coin/builds but before setBusinessList and setTaskInfo save the rest of the same checkpoint.
findings.evidence: Actual saveGame interrupted after its first durable write restores round2/coin77/new building level, but previous business weapon0 and task index0/stage0 instead of weapon1/task index1/stage2.
findings.minimalFix: Construct the entire battle checkpoint in memory and persist once. Preserve current data shape and unknown fields; do not expose half a checkpoint through setters that each write.
findings.tests: Interrupt/fail each checkpoint boundary; the durable record must be either the complete old snapshot or complete new snapshot, never mixed.

findings.title: Sidebar one-time reward is outside the claim journal
findings.trigger: Sidebar reward sets standalone SIDE_BOARD_REWARD cache flag before adding gold and ignores failure of that flag write.
findings.evidence: Actual registered reward callback, authored reward2000: interruption immediately after successful flag save gives persisted flag1 and gold0 forever. When only flag writes fail, two callbacks award4000 with flag still missing.
findings.minimalFix: Move the once-only claim marker into the existing staged reward journal (e.g. GuideData time key), honoring the old standalone flag for legacy already-claimed saves. Ensure marker and gold/counters commit together; do not award when journaling fails.
findings.tests: Every write interruption, blocked marker storage, repeat callback, and migration from legacy flag1: reward and marker recover once, with no duplicate or lost gold.

findings.trigger: Two overlapping cloud/identity requests, a transport failure, or a malformed response.
findings.evidence: Two POST calls create one XMLHttpRequest; the second overwrites its handlers and the first callback is lost. DONE followed by error completes the newer callback twice. Invalid JSON with HTTP200 invokes callback({code:0}), which both save adapters interpret as success. A fresh Sf GET has timeout0, so initial cloud login can wait indefinitely.
findings.minimalFix: Use one XHR per request, a guarded terminal completion shared by DONE/error/timeout, and a finite GET deadline. Keep JSON parse errors separate from consumer callback exceptions. Report malformed responses as failures using the existing error shape; preserve documented successful empty-body behavior if required by the backend contract.
findings.test: Concurrent requests retain their own callbacks and payloads; network event combinations complete once; malformed JSON never reports code0; stalled GET reaches a terminal callback.

findings.trigger: Two queued saveData operations for the same key before the queue starts.
findings.evidence: With later timestamps, newest payload is sent but only the oldest caller completes. With equal millisecond timestamps, the newest payload is discarded and the old value is sent; the queue is then empty. This loses the latest cloud snapshot during a burst.
findings.minimalFix: Coalesce by enqueue order rather than strict millisecond comparison and preserve completion callbacks for every coalesced task. Complete all accepted callers exactly once with the outcome of the retained latest snapshot.
findings.test: Same-key saves with equal timestamps send the last value; each caller completes once. Different keys/URLs retain queue order.

findings.trigger: SfTrackHttp returns its normal transport error object {code:-1} to a task with maxRetries3.
findings.evidence: Task.run tests truthiness, treating the error object as success. Probe completed after one attempt, retained tryCount3, and scheduled no retry.
findings.minimalFix: Distinguish transport/parse failure from an application response while retaining terminal application codes such as -2/-10 for their existing handlers. Retry bounded transient failures only; deliver the final failure once.
findings.test: Transport failure retries to the configured limit; terminal application errors are not hidden/retried indefinitely; successful save completes once.

findings.trigger: XHR becomes DONE with status0, then emits its error/timeout event.
findings.evidence: Both GET and POST invoke the caller twice. GET also leaves timeout0. Existing FeedPlayableMgr failure callbacks enqueue retries, so duplicate completion can duplicate retry work on its supported platform.
findings.minimalFix: Guard completion once per XHR while preserving existing GET(bool,text) and POST(text-or-null) signatures. Set a finite GET deadline without changing POST's existing 7000ms default.
findings.test: DONE+error and DONE+timeout invoke one callback, and successful payloads retain their current shape.

findings.trigger: Cloud load returns code-2, or save returns code-10.
findings.evidence: Both adapters show the intended modal and update canUpdate/isOpened, but never complete their load/save callback. Loading's cloud-init dependency therefore has no terminal state. Each adapter probe showed zero load and zero save callbacks despite receiving final responses.
findings.minimalFix: Preserve account restriction, disabled saving, modal and exit behavior. Supply an explicit exactly-once failure completion/terminal startup state, rather than silently continuing as a successful cloud load. Root must decide whether the existing callback API can express this without weakening the restriction.
findings.test: Each restriction response completes failure exactly once while retaining its restriction state and modal/exit behavior; success remains unchanged.

findings.trigger: Call init twice while the first cloud login/load is pending.
findings.evidence: The second callback fires immediately before authentication or cloud data load, because isInited is set when initialization starts. The first callback finishes later. Current Loading calls init once, so this is a coalesced-caller robustness issue.
findings.minimalFix: Separate pending initialization from ready state and queue concurrent completion callbacks until the single load resolves. Avoid issuing duplicate login/load requests or changing stored formats.
findings.test: Two concurrent init callers wait for one load; already-ready init remains immediate; terminal failure drains pending callers consistently.

findings.title: Stop Server can forcibly terminate an unrelated process
findings.trigger: A different Windows process occupies the configured bridge port; press Stop Server when the plugin has no owned child process.
findings.evidence: The actual IPC handler, run with mocked net and child_process, returned managed:false and called taskkill /PID 424242 /T /F on the mocked unowned listener. No real process was killed.
findings.impact: Can kill unrelated applications/process trees and lose their unsaved work.
findings.minimalFix: Stop only the child process this extension launched and still owns. Report an unmanaged listener without killing it; remove the port-to-PID fallback or require separately verified ownership.
findings.test: Mock an occupied port with no owned child and assert zero taskkill/process.kill calls; verify the owned-child stop path still works.

findings.title: Localization save can overwrite a concurrent external edit
findings.trigger: Another editor changes catalog.json after the initial revision read, while this save prepares its temporary output.
findings.evidence: An isolated fs wrapper injected external unknown:77 after the temp-file write. _backupAndSave then renamed its stale output and restored unknown:1 without a conflict error.
findings.impact: Silently loses external/concurrent catalog edits, contrary to the project revision-protection requirement.
findings.minimalFix: Use a unique temporary filename, re-read and compare the exact current revision immediately before rename, and retain drafts on mismatch. Preserve untouched bytes with the existing JSONDocument patch helper.
findings.test: Inject a concurrent change during temporary output preparation and assert cancellation, unchanged external bytes, retained draft and no stale-temp overwrite.

findings.title: Composite battle settings bypass numeric validation
findings.trigger: Set StaminaSupply to -5,15 using its numeric component field. The frontend gives composite fields no minimum, and the backend skips numeric validation for every string containing a comma or semicolon.
findings.evidence: Actual Schema.validate against current A/B/D/catalog documents reports zero ParameterCfg errors for -5,15. KinghtFallUIAddStrength parses the values with Number and calls addPowerNum(-5) after the ordinary purchase deducts gems; that method directly adds the negative value.
findings.impact: An apparently valid saved authoring change makes a refill charge gems while removing stamina. AddDesktop and ButtonUnlock tuples likewise lack shape/reference constraints.
findings.minimalFix: Validate known composite parameter formats by enumKey, with finite/integer/nonnegative bounds and valid goods IDs where applicable. Preserve the authored ButtonUnlock -1 sentinel and existing unusual/out-of-range legacy values as advisory when untouched; do not normalize defaults.
findings.test: Reject newly authored negative/malformed stamina rewards and invalid reward tuples; verify all current saved settings and untouched sentinel values remain accepted/advisory exactly as before.

findings.title: A rejected character/item draft permanently blocks later corrected edits
findings.trigger: Make a validation-invalid edit such as targeting a slot already used by another part, then correct the slot and Save.
findings.evidence: Executing the actual extracted stage function with a rejected first payload and valid corrected payload produced only one IPC call. stageError is rethrown before every later change; Save rethrows it, and only Discard clears it.
findings.impact: Users cannot save corrected character/item work without discarding their local draft. The shared client affects both editors.
findings.minimalFix: Allow later corrected payloads to retry at the last accepted revision and clear validation errors on success. Handle true stale-version conflicts separately without silently overwriting another panel's draft. Update lastSent only when appropriate so failed payloads can be retried.
findings.test: Reject a duplicate-slot draft, correct it, and verify a subsequent change and Save succeed while preserving the rest of the draft; also retain explicit conflict behavior for stale revisions.

findings.title: A transient character catalog load failure disables all looks for the session
findings.trigger: character-parts/catalog loads successfully but characters/catalog fails once.
findings.evidence: Three actual bind calls after an injected characters/catalog error generated only one catalog request. library is set and loading remains true, so load() can never retry.
findings.impact: Assigned looks never apply until a full page/session reload despite later successful resource availability.
findings.minimalFix: Track success/loading for each catalog separately; clear loading on every completion and permit bounded retry when a required catalog is absent, without resetting valid loaded data or equipping inactive actors.
findings.test: Fail the second catalog once, recover on a later bind/retry, and verify the assigned look applies while no part textures/appearance mutations occur on inactive units.

findings.title: An unchanged localization Save still rewrites the catalog and builds artwork
findings.trigger: Send the current unchanged catalog and revision to Save, including an edit-revert operation whose panel dirty flag remains set.
findings.evidence: _backupAndSave rewrote an isolated unchanged catalog, changed unknown numeric spelling 1.00 to 1, and created a backup. The save handler subsequently calls compile and asset refresh unconditionally.
findings.impact: Violates no-op save requirements and causes unnecessary reimports/rebuilds/backups; unlike the newer stores, untouched bytes are not preserved.
findings.minimalFix: Detect semantic equality before any filesystem write, backup, artwork compile or refresh; return a noChanges result compatible with the panel. Use patch-based serialization for actual edits.
findings.test: Assert unchanged and edit-revert saves preserve bytes/mtime and invoke no backup, compiler or assetdb refresh; actual edits still produce verified backups.

findings.title: The root test command excludes 14 editor regression suites
findings.trigger: Run npm test / npm run check expecting the advertised project-wide validation.
findings.evidence: The discovery roots are tools and packages/localization-editor/test only. Thirteen packages/game-data-editor/test/*.test.js files and packages/game-data-editor/testing/client.test.js are never selected. The reproduction lists exact omissions.
findings.impact: Save/revision/recovery, asset validation, map editing, timing-default preservation and managed-test-session regressions can ship while the root command reports all groups passed.
findings.minimalFix: Include the game-data-editor test and testing directories, or invoke their existing runner as an explicit root check group. Add a discovery regression test.
findings.test: Verify those fourteen files are discovered and that a failing fixture makes the root command fail; run the expanded suite without changing authored data.

findings.title: Popup tweens retain destroyed panels for the lifetime of the game
findings.trigger: Repeatedly open and close uncached Pop panels such as Settings, Pause, or Online Rewards.
findings.evidence: getTween stores each tween in the singleton twenMap by the newly instantiated node UUID. BaseUI.openAni/closeAni call it; BaseUI defaults cache=false and UIMgr.closeUI destroys uncached nodes. No external caller invokes stopTween. Creator 2.4.13 Tween retains its _target and actions after completion or stop. The isolated actual TweenMgr probe retained 100 destroyed-node targets after 100 cycles.
findings.impact: The map and callback/target references grow on every new popup instance, keeping dead UI object graphs reachable and adding memory pressure over long sessions.
findings.minimalFix: Make ownership weak (node-keyed WeakMap) if enumeration is unnecessary, or explicitly release this manager's tween entries when the owning UI is destroyed. Preserve stop/replace behavior for a currently active node; do not stop unrelated tweens or change animation timing.
findings.test: Repeated uncached panel teardown must not accumulate strong manager entries. Replacing a tween on the same live node must still stop exactly the older owned tween.

findings.title: Virtual lists instantiate every new row twice and retain the discarded localized clone
findings.trigger: Open an active virtual list with an empty pool, or scroll far enough to need a new row. OnlineReward, Achievement and Passport prefabs use this class.
findings.evidence: The empty-pool branch first assigns cc.instantiate(_itemTmp), then !(n && cc.isValid(e)) is always true because n=false, so it instantiates again. The first clone is neither used nor destroyed. A combined actual List+LanguageMgr VM probe creates two clones for one row and confirms that the unused clone's label stays in LanguageMgr._labels. OnlineReward and Achievement template descendants contain localized label tokens, so the global localization hook makes this an active retention path.
findings.impact: Doubles new-row instantiation work and retains abandoned localized row trees; later language refreshes keep revisiting those invisible labels.
findings.minimalFix: Take an item from the pool if available, then instantiate once only when that result is absent/invalid. Keep the reuse flag accurate for widget alignment; do not change row layout or data.
findings.test: Assert one fresh clone per empty/invalid pool result, zero fresh clones for a valid pooled item, and no extra tracked localization labels.

findings.title: Listener mutation skips live subscribers and duplicate removal leaves registrations
findings.evidence: Self-removing A prevents B from receiving the same event. Emitting uses the live array and off splices forward. Array registry also collides with inherited property event names.
findings.fix: Use an own-key registry and a stable dispatch snapshot, skip subscriptions removed during dispatch, defer new subscriptions to next dispatch; remove all requested duplicate registrations.

findings.title: Resource cache repeatedly consumes release credits and loses them on reload
findings.evidence: An asset with one pending release and one live owner reaches refCount0 after two cleanup periods. Loading the same key replaces pending release credits. getAssets always returns null. Releasing a permanent owner twice consumes another owner's reference.
findings.fix: Consume each release credit once, preserve existing accounting, implement asset lookup, detach released owner lists before decRef, keep temporary/permanent accounting coherent, retain SpriteFrame type for remote SpriteFrame requests.

findings.title: Late asset callbacks leak references and cross closed UI lifetimes
findings.evidence: Late load after BaseCtrl.onDestroy adds a key to a list that was already released. Close/reopen BaseUI accepts callbacks from the previous open. BaseMgr.onDestroy retains event handlers.
findings.fix: Track asynchronous ownership by lifecycle, immediately release references arriving after close/destruction, fence reopen callbacks, clear owned events during teardown. Preserve cache ownership until destruction.

findings.title: UI initializer and consumer exceptions strand the opening queue and input block
findings.evidence: Actual init and user-callback exceptions each leave isopening=true with one queued UI; final input event remains block=false.
findings.fix: Finalize opening ownership on all exception paths, remove partially initialized instances and restore transition/input before draining. Preserve callback errors for diagnostics.

findings.title: Decision callbacks can execute more than once or after closing
findings.evidence: Start optional-ad offer, decline/close it, then deliver ad success: callback sequence is false,true for a single decision. Build choices and retry callbacks similarly remain callable until scheduled removal.
findings.fix: One completion per decision lifetime, reject closed/destroyed/stale callbacks and repeat taps; preserve declined/canceled semantics and allow ad retry on failure.

findings.title: Detached pool templates survive pool teardown; pool watermark admits an extra node
findings.evidence: Active gameplay callers pass detached cc.instantiate(prefab) templates. destory clears the NodePool but never destroys or clears its detached template. Watermark check uses < rather than >= and duplicate over-cap returns may destroy a node already pooled.
findings.fix: Release only pool-owned detached templates, preserve authored parented templates; enforce capacity exactly and reject duplicate returns before destruction. Verify with actual installed NodePool.

findings.expected: One retained health-bar component per unit

findings.regression: Cold load, pool/reinitialize before completion, deliver original callback once; assert exactly one bar, current HP, and no attachment to destroyed owner.

findings.trigger: Damage a soldier or building while its asynchronous health-bar prefab is not loaded
findings.expected: Apply combat damage successfully; deferred health-bar callback should show current health
findings.minimalFix: Keep health-bar presentation optional until its asynchronous load completes. Damage, death and combat transitions must proceed even without the HP component; completion renders current state.
findings.regression: Damage/recover/kill while HP prefab remains pending, then complete load and verify HP and lifecycle without throws.

findings.trigger: The last in-range enemy dies or leaves between hero attack windup and its damage event; attack cancellation at a round/restart boundary can leave the same latch
findings.expected: Finish/cancel the attack cycle and resume acquiring enemies after cooldown
findings.minimalFix: Release the attack in-flight latch even when damage event finds no target; reset attack timer when restart/end-of-round cancels a scheduled attack. Preserve saved timing event positions and cooldown.
findings.regression: Acquire then lose last target during windup; complete damage/animation; introduce new target and assert attack resumes. Cancel at end-round and both restart variants without leaving timer -1.

findings.trigger: An enemy shot is bound to the hero before hero death, then survives until the same hero node revives
findings.expected: Dead/reborn hero invalidates shots fired at the previous life, like enemy and soldier targets
findings.minimalFix: Register hero combat actor and life generation using the same node contract as enemies/allies. Invalidate life identity when death/restart/initialization ends a life, including before a delayed shot can resolve.
findings.regression: Actual hero dead/reborn transitions invalidate retained normal/enemy08 shots; fresh shot at new living hero still hits once. Preserve game epoch checks.

findings.trigger: Call dormant public KinghtFallGameMap.findPath/findPath2 with an unreachable goal and a reachable two-cell cycle
findings.expected: Finite search returns no path; coordinate identity must be stable rather than allocating new node keys on every visit
findings.activeUse: No current source imports or calls KinghtFallGameMap; current gameplay uses NavigationGrid
findings.minimalFix: Use stable coordinate identities/canonical nodes in the dormant path search and a bounded termination rule; do not replace the active NavigationGrid.
findings.regression: Unreachable 2-cell cycle must terminate; reachable route and existing fallback contract remain valid.

findings.trigger: Remove/expire a DamageCut buff before its cold effect-prefab request completes
findings.expected: Late buff resources must be returned instead of attaching an unowned permanent effect; actor pooling/destruction also invalidates callbacks
findings.minimalFix: Before applying delayed buff effect, verify owner validity/lifetime and that the captured buff is still owned. Return an obsolete node to its pool rather than attaching it. Do not change art or effect styling.
findings.regression: Expire/remove buff or pool/destroy actor before cold callback; assert no orphan child and correct pool return. Current valid buff still receives exactly one effect.

findings.trigger: Register two audio IDs with the same path in different bundles, then play them in sequence
findings.expected: Clip-cache identity includes both bundle and path
findings.activeUse: Public audio API defect; current shipped main/GAD config paths do not collide
findings.minimalFix: Use an unambiguous bundle-plus-path key consistently for asset caching and coalescing; keep playback channel keys separate.
findings.regression: Two bundles with identical relative paths produce two distinct clips; repeated same bundle/path coalesces; no audio/storage real calls.

findings.trigger: Exit the legacy app while its first data/preload callback is pending, then complete that callback
findings.expected: Exit releases its touch blocker and invalidates pending enter callbacks
findings.activeUse: Legacy app public lifecycle; current main battle does not call GAD_App
findings.minimalFix: Track enter generation and owned touch-blocker; exit invalidates pending callbacks and releases its blocker. Stale data/preload/UI completion cannot reset player state, open UI or start audio.
findings.regression: Exit during each asynchronous enter phase; deliver stale callbacks; no reopen/reset/music or retained touch block. New enter still succeeds.

findings.trigger: Apply a patch containing only an English entry or a width change to an existing label style
findings.expected: Merge only explicitly patched properties; preserve Chinese, context, other style fields and unknown metadata
findings.minimalFix: Use validated property-level patch semantics, preserving untouched keys; explicitly specify replacement/removal if intended rather than inferring it from omission.

findings.trigger: Apply an empty patch (or a semantically identical patch)
findings.expected: No-op save performs zero writes and preserves original bytes
findings.minimalFix: Compare patch semantics before serialization/backup; exit without mutation if nothing changes.

findings.trigger: Another panel saves the catalog after merge-patch reads it and before the CLI writes its replacement
findings.expected: Revision conflict aborts without overwriting newer catalog contents
findings.minimalFix: Capture original bytes/hash, validate complete merged result, recheck revision immediately before atomic commit and preserve backup of the exact accepted revision.

findings.trigger: Destroy/leave the Main scene while its initial UITop load is pending, then complete the old UI callback
findings.expected: Old startup callbacks must stop once their Main instance is destroyed; a new scene owns its own startup chain.
findings.minimalFix: Guard every startup continuation with Main lifetime/generation validity; invalidate generation on destruction. Do not close unrelated/new scene UI.

findings.trigger: Destroy Loading before the asynchronous version-check callback completes
findings.expected: Obsolete startup must not initiate server/user initialization after destruction.
findings.minimalFix: Check loading-instance validity/generation before starting initServer, as well as inside its completion; keep retry terminal failure behavior.

findings.trigger: Move either active settings volume slider to its minimum value0
findings.expected: Zero volume must remain zero and mute that channel without changing the other channel.
findings.minimalFix: Preserve0 as a valid volume in setters, initialization and playback; use explicit undefined checks rather than truthy volume fallback. Tests must cover reload and pending/new sources without actual audio.

findings.trigger: Two startup failures are queued and the first retry throws synchronously (for example an immediate cached-resource consumer throws)
findings.expected: One failing retry must not silently discard all other pending retries.
findings.minimalFix: Run each queued retry with exception-safe iteration, preserve/report the failed retry as appropriate, and allow other operations to retry; do not mask the exception as successful loading.

findings.title: Completing a battle drops the receipt for a still-pending reward journal and resurrects its checkpoint on reload
findings.trigger: A permanent in-battle task reward journals GameData, all target writes succeed, but clearing rewardJournal fails. The current battle then completes before that cleanup succeeds.
findings.evidence: Actual claimRewards/setCheckpoint/beginSettlement and actual preload sequence: task gives123 gold, battle gives50, completed GameData levelNum=-1. Reload installs old level1 round3 checkpoint from pending journal because GameData rewardTransaction was discarded; finishing again gives50 more (173 ->223). User and Mission receipts survive, GameData receipt does not.
findings.minimalFix: Preserve GameData reward-transaction receipt across checkpoint reset/completion, or serialize pending journal recovery with reset so an acknowledged checkpoint can never be reinstalled after its battle finishes. Apply the same invariant to setNewGame. Do not drop newer progress while retrying the cleanup.
findings.regression: Fail only rewardJournal deletion, complete the active battle, reload through actual preload, retry recovery repeatedly; game remains completed and cannot grant another settlement. Also reset/restart with pending cleanup.

findings.title: Battle settlement silently discards supported relic wave rewards
findings.trigger: An authored WaveReward contains an existing Type02 goods/relic ID. The editor explicitly exposes and accepts all GoodsCfg IDs for wave rewards; current shipped waves contain only currencies/pass points, so their defaults are unaffected.
findings.evidence: WaveReward [[2006,1]] passes actual editor schema; actual beginSettlement completes and clears the run, yet getTreasureLevel(120001) stays null. The actual addRewards control correctly unlocks that same relic at level1.
findings.minimalFix: Make idempotent battle settlement support the same configured permanent goods as addRewards, including relic unlock/fragments/overflow conversion. Keep reward conversion and its achievement effects in the receipt-protected atomic award, rather than calling independent saving APIs after settlement is acknowledged.
findings.regression: First copy, duplicate fragments, maxed relic conversion, doubled settlement, and interrupted/retried settlement with a valid relic wave reward; ordinary authored gold/pass points remain unchanged.

findings.title: Challenge chest eligibility uses its display index instead of configured challenge ID
findings.trigger: The supported Challenge array is reordered or shortened; e.g [3,1,2]. Existing shipped arrays [1,2,3] mask the bug.
findings.evidence: Actual editor schema accepts [3,1,2]. With only Pass completed (mask1), actual onBoxClick(0) grants123 gold for challenge3 (castle unharmed), despite that bit being unset. initMapView and hasGetLevelReward already use the configured challenge ID and disagree with the handler.

findings.title: Mini-app clearAll leaves authoritative in-memory saves alive and the next save restores them to disk
findings.trigger: WECHAT or BYTEDANCE calls CacheUtils.clearAll, then the process remains alive long enough to read/save (e.g server clearing is asynchronous or mini-app restart is delayed/failed).
findings.evidence: Both actual platform branches: disk after clear is {}, but getData(progress) still returns old from sffile. Saving unrelated fresh=new serializes stale sffile and restores old progress to disk. No real SDK/file access used.
findings.minimalFix: Reset the authoritative sffile dictionary together with its persisted file while preserving the requested retained keys/identity keys. Handle failed clearing explicitly; do not continue as if data was removed when the authoritative write failed.
findings.regression: Both host branches with delayed restart: clear, read, unrelated save, and simulated reload cannot resurrect progress; retained keys survive; failed authoritative clear is reported and does not partially claim success.

findings.title: Legacy guide numeric alias fails to round-trip through Utils

findings.title: Virtual list can omit incoming rows while a touched outgoing row is retained
findings.trigger: Drag starts on a list row and moves the viewport by a row while its visible row count remains unchanged. _scrollItem intentionally keeps the touched outgoing node in the pool bookkeeping.
findings.evidence: Actual _onScrolling/_delRedundantItem: initial children/cache[0,1,2], requested viewport[1,2,3], touched0 retained ->same cached length3, no _createOrUpdateItem calls and row3 absent. Control without retained0 creates[1,2,3]. Current Passport, OnlineReward and Achievement prefabs use virtual List; Creator2.4.13 CCScrollView marks its synthetic cancel simulate=true, which List deliberately ignores.
findings.minimalFix: Check changed visible ID endpoints/set independently of count equality, and treat a retained touched offscreen row separately from visible completion. Preserve touch ownership and bounded pooling.
findings.regression: Scroll both directions while holding a recycled row; incoming IDs instantiate even when item counts match. Verify no unnecessary rerenders for unchanged visible IDs, and deferred frame-by-frame mode still completes.

findings.title: Interrupted animated list removal loses its index and can invoke the removal callback twice
findings.trigger: aniDelItem(index,callback) is in progress when the List is disabled and re-enabled. No current production callers of this API were found, so this is a dormant component contract defect.

findings.minimalFix: Keep the requested index with the pending deletion, and use one completion owner/guard shared by ordinary completion and lifecycle recovery. Cancel/ignore stale animation completion after recovery.
findings.regression: Disable/re-enable before either removal animation phase completes; callback is invoked once with original index, even if old delayed callback is delivered afterward.

findings.title: Artwork rebuild can overwrite concurrent output changes and leave a partially replaced set after a write failure
findings.reachability: Both explicit Rebuild saved artwork and every changed Save tables request call this compiler. Main serializes its own builds, but the asynchronous render phase permits external catalog, source-image/font, or generated-output edits. A busy/locked destination is an ordinary filesystem failure while replacing multiple outputs.
findings.trigger: Start a build; while its mocked renderer is pending replace the fixture catalog and generated PNG, then resolve the original render. Separately inject EBUSY on replacement of the second PNG.
findings.evidence: The actual compile method reported success and replaced a concurrently edited output with the older rendered result while the catalog held the newer translation. The second probe rejected EBUSY after replacing the first output, leaving the second at its old contents and its .tmp file present. No output backup or rollback exists. The catalog's own save is backed up and revision checked; these protections do not cover the artifact writes.
findings.minimalFix: Capture the relevant input/output revisions before asynchronous render, stage and validate all output bytes before replacement, recheck revisions before committing, and preserve output backups with verified rollback on partial failure. Use unique staging paths and clean them on failure. Retain exact unchanged bytes and the existing no-op save behavior.
regressions: Pending render plus concurrent output replacement rejects without overwriting that replacement.
Catalog/source revision change during rendering cannot install stale artwork as a successful current build.
Second-output replacement failure restores already replaced files and cleans temporary files without altering external changes.
A successful unchanged rebuild performs no output writes; no-op Save tables does not invoke a build.
findings.limits: Renderer execution is mocked; no Electron/browser/editor process or real source asset was opened. Synthetic PNG signatures are sufficient for the real compiler's write-validation branch. This is an authoring transaction issue, not a runtime UI-style finding. Catalog+artwork have intentionally separate success/warning reporting; the finding does not require undoing a successfully saved catalog when artwork rendering fails.

findings.trigger: Refresh/select home stages repeatedly, or reopen the sidebar reward popup. A pending home preview load may also finish after its controller is destroyed.
findings.evidence: Actual ResourceMgr.loadRes defaults to permanent acquisition and addRef on every request/cache hit. These direct callers supply neither a release key nor BaseCtrl/BaseUI ownership. Twenty home refreshes leave 20 asset references after destruction and cache expiry; ten sidebar instances leave 10. A delayed actual home callback accesses an already destroyed owner. The owned loadResFromBundle negative control releases all 20 references.
findings.impact: Unbounded retained asset references during normal repeated home use; stale home completion may throw while touching destroyed UI. Memory size/FPS impact was not measured.
findings.minimalFix: Route the home SkeletonData acquisition through inherited loadResFromBundle and sidebar SpriteFrame through inherited loadSpriteFrame. Retain the existing owner-generation and release semantics. For same-owner stage races, a current-selection guard may be appropriate but the visual-only mismatch is not separately counted.
findings.regression: Use actual resource/cache/base-owner methods, repeated cold/cache-hit acquisitions and screen destruction, delayed success/failure after close; assert zero refs after cache expiry and no stale callback/recovery prompt.

findings.title: Repeat treasure draws detach old reward items without releasing their owned assets
findings.trigger: Finish a treasure reveal, then use the dialog repeat-draw button. Old ItemGood/ItemTreasure nodes have acquired their own icon references.
findings.evidence: getReward calls removeAllChildren. The actual Creator 2.4.13 method only cleans actions and clears parents; it does not destroy item components or return them to a pool. Actual BaseCtrl-owned icon ref remains 1 after detachment and cache expiry, then becomes 0 if the abandoned child is explicitly destroyed. The detached item is no longer a child of the dialog, so later dialog destruction cannot release it.
findings.impact: Repeated draws abandon item resource credits and consume pooled nodes without returning them, retaining assets for the session. Reward transaction correctness is unaffected.
findings.minimalFix: Dispose replaced reward nodes through a defined owner: return known pooled ItemGood nodes safely or destroy replaced nodes and let their BaseCtrl destructor release refs. Avoid discarding child references solely with removeAllChildren; keep authored reveal timing and reward calculations unchanged.
findings.regression: Exercise actual getReward across repeated draws with item-owned icon loads; verify every replaced item is pooled or destroyed, stale pending draw completions cannot attach abandoned generation items, and closing/repeating leaves bounded references.

findings.trigger: First-time guide prefab load fails; player chooses Cancel in ResourceMgr recovery.
findings.evidence: guide-cancel-results.json actual GuildCfg/UIMgr/ResourceMgr/UITouch chain leaves sole legacy input claim, zero guide instance and empty queue after cancellation.
findings.minimalFix: Give the guide request a releasable input owner and release on cancel/abandon/invalid owner, while retry preserves the intended guide acquisition. Avoid global unblock of unrelated owners.
findings.reachability: Active tutorial callers in KinghtFallUIHome/UIGame/UIBuff; resource failure path.

findings.title: Adding a language erases existing translation fields for that locale
findings.trigger: A valid catalog contains previously prepared fr strings while fr is not yet listed in languages. Add fr in the translation panel.
findings.evidence: localization-panel-results.json: entry.greeting.fr changes from Bonjour to an empty string; the catalog passes Catalog.structure before and after. The operation dirties the draft, so the next explicit Save persists the erasure.
findings.reachability: Explicit authoring action on a supported version1 catalog with preserved additional locale/extension fields. No claim that current shipped English/Chinese player data already contains this case.
findings.minimalFix: Preflight the whole operation. Initialize only absent locale fields; preserve existing strings. Reject an incompatible non-string extension-field collision before mutating the draft.
findings.tests: Actual _addLanguage regression for prefilled locale text, absent fields, unknown non-string collision, no partial mutation, and an unchanged catalog until explicit Save.

findings.title: A delayed Reload response silently discards edits made while loading
findings.trigger: Click Reload in an already-open translation panel, then type a new translation before the IPC load reply arrives. Text fields remain editable.
findings.evidence: localization-panel-results.json: the actual _load/_changed/_writeDraft path changes Typed after requesting reload back to Hello, resets dirty=false and writes no recovery draft.
findings.reachability: Normal asynchronous editor IPC; the Reload confirmation only authorized discarding work that existed when clicked. This finding concerns later accepted user edits.
findings.minimalFix: Track a load generation and draft edit revision. Apply a response only if its request is still current and the draft has not changed since the request, otherwise retain the newer draft and surface that reload was superseded. Preserve initial load/no-op behavior.
findings.tests: Deferred actual panel IPC: edit during reload, overlapping loads resolved out of order, normal reload, and panel closure while a reply is pending.

findings.title: A valid trailing spawn-delay group prevents wave completion and throws in the queue HUD
findings.trigger: Save a custom row 1#90001,1;-1,2 using supported game-data authoring; kill its final actual enemy before the delay groups drain.
findings.evidence: Actual Schema.validate accepts the row. Actual delEnemy calls tryEndGame while the queue is nonempty; actual onUpdata drains the final delay but never checks completion. After60s there are no enemies/groups yet no RoundEnd; explicit tryEndGame emits it. Actual UIGame.update dereferences e[1].id when only one -1 group remains.
findings.impact: Custom valid waves can permanently stop progression; exception is repeated until the delay empties. Existing checked-in wave rows do not currently use this trailing sequence.
findings.minimalFix: Check normal wave completion after a spawn batch changes the queue to empty, retaining pendingEnemySpawns/_roundCompleted guards. For the indicator, safely find the next non-delay group or hide if absent; do not modify authored rows or spawn timing.
findings.regression: Actual-method tests: last enemy dies before tail delay; multiple delay groups; pending asynchronous spawn still blocks completion; exactly one RoundEnd/GameOver; empty upcoming-unit HUD does not throw.

findings.observation: An explicitly supplied nonexistent COCOS_ENGINE_DIR registers the actual Box2D integration as skipped. This can hide a misconfigured machine expected to execute contact integration.

proof.name: real Box2D shield contacts release the captured opposing gate pair and both reach their rally goals

findings.recommendation: When touching optional-engine test plumbing, distinguish absent default installation from an invalid explicit configuration, as build-collider-lifecycle already does. This is test coverage plumbing, not a gameplay defect.

findings.title: Cancelling failed branch-choice load leaves a paid upgrade and permanently paused battle
findings.trigger: Stand long enough to buy a branched building upgrade; UIBuildSel prefab fails to load, then choose Cancel in ResourceMgr recovery.
findings.evidence: Actual BuildBase.doUpgrade + UIMgr.open + ResourceMgr.loadRes/resolveRuntimeRecovery: coin20→15, canStart=false, only GamePause(true), no chooser instance, director resumed. Upgrade callback never runs, so gameplay pause never clears.
findings.reachability: Active gameplay failure/cancel path. Authored ArrowTower/Barracks/PrivateHouse/Mill/Wall have multi-choice BranchBuild levels. No invalid config or unsupported caller required.
findings.minimalFix: Make the purchase/pause a single owned operation with an explicit cancellation result from the UI opening flow. Cancel releases only this game pause and restores the pending purchase/stand state, or defer debit until a successful single selection. Retrying must not debit twice; ignore completion after building/battle lifetime changes.
regressions: Failed chooser + Cancel leaves coin/level unchanged and gameplay/start control usable.
Failure + Retry + one selection spends once and upgrades once.
Battle restart/building destruction while chooser pending cannot mutate new battle or release an unrelated pause.
findings.scopeNote: Backend purchase/recovery only; no styling/layout repair.

findings.title: Resuming a checkpoint grants first-wave silver achievement progress again
findings.trigger: Reopen an existing battle checkpoint.
findings.evidence: Actual new GameCtrlData constructor/initData/loadMonster runs before actual GameCtrl.loadGame/setRound; the subsequent onRestart(false) subtracts/adds the saved current-wave reward, not the constructor wave1 award. Three Map01 wave6 resumes preserve coin77/round6 but permanent GetSliver totals increase6→12→18, with9 mission save calls. Authored Map01 first StartSliver is6.
findings.reachability: Normal checkpoint Continue flow from UIGame.start. Coin replay from saved one-shot buffs was fixed earlier; this distinct initial-wave achievement write remains.
findings.minimalFix: Distinguish fresh-battle initialization from checkpoint restoration before awarding initial-wave currency/progression. Restore queues/derived data without acquisition-only achievement writes. Preserve fresh game and real new-wave/restart semantics and save format.
regressions: Resume same authored checkpoint repeatedly: saved coin and persistent achievement unchanged.
Fresh battle earns initial StartSliver exactly once.
Normal subsequent wave earns its StartSliver once; retry current wave does not add net achievement progress.

findings.title: Legacy exit during pending gameplay prefab load still installs a late game UI
findings.trigger: Call GAD_App.enter_App after preload, call exit_App while UIMgr is loading GAD_UIGame, then deliver the outstanding prefab.
findings.evidence: Actual GAD_App + UIMgr + ResourceMgr chain: exit callback once, entry callback zero, audio calls zero, but late prefab registers an active UIGame after exit. Generation guard only checks the completion callback after show() already instantiated, initialized and activated the component; closeById at exit had no registered instance to close.
findings.reachability: Dormant legacy app public enter/exit cancellation contract. No claim of a current main-game player path. Prior generation fix correctly blocks audio/callbacks but does not cancel UI construction.
findings.minimalFix: Own and cancel/invalidate the pending open before prefab instantiation, or dispose exactly the stale node supplied to completion. Guard new entry sessions so an old completion cannot close the replacement game. Preserve unrelated UIs and callback once semantics.
regressions: Exit while pending resource leaves no active/registered legacy UI after late success.
Exit/re-enter with reversed old/new completions preserves only current UI.
Exit while already displayed still cleans up once and remains silent.

findings.title: Live diagnostic waveFinished can latch before final asynchronous enemy spawn arrives
findings.trigger: Live fixture drains its last enemy queue entry while its prefab is still loading.
findings.evidence: Actual GameCtrlData.onUpdata(.6) + actual GameCtrl.addEnemy on a one-unit final queue leaves pendingEnemySpawns1 and queue0. Fixture replacement tryEndGame sets _liveWaveFinished=true; identical production tryEndGame correctly does not finish. Flag stays latched while spawned enemy can remain alive.
findings.reachability: Temporary debug live fixture only, used for later-wave acceptance reporting. No production wave guard regression. This does not by itself invalidate prior observed battle movement/combat evidence.
findings.minimalFix: Keep the production completion predicate, including pendingEnemySpawns, when suppressing scenario-ending UI. Reset pending diagnostic state consistently when intentionally cancelling a scenario. Do not mutate authored waves or game progress.
regressions: Pending final prefab cannot mark finished.
Last live enemy death after successful spawn marks completion.
Trailing delay groups still finish once fully drained with no pending spawns.
Scenario cancellation followed by a new wave does not inherit an old pending or finished state.

findings.title: An older Save acknowledgement replaces a newer disk revision and invalidates the recovery draft
trigger: Save draft B; catalog B is written, artwork finishes, but Creator asset refresh acknowledgement is still pending.
Reload B, edit and save C. The compile queue is ordered, but refresh acknowledgement callbacks are independent.
Acknowledge C, then type unsaved D, then acknowledge old B.
findings.observed: The panel unconditionally assigns the old B revision and writes draft D with that stale revision even though the current disk catalog is C. Next Save rejects the disk mismatch, and after reopening/reloading, Restore draft rejects D as belonging to an older disk revision. D is still present in recovery storage; this is blocked normal recovery/save, not proven irreversible data loss.
findings.proof: Actual panel _save/_load/_changed/_writeDraft/_restoreDraft plus actual main backupAndSave/queued compile/save handlers. Only compile and assetdb refresh are inert; filesystem writes stay in the ignored audit fixture.
findings.control: Typing during a single pending Save retains unsaved edits and writes a recovery draft whose revision matches the disk, as intended.
findings.minimalFix: Give Save acknowledgements/error handlers explicit current-request and draft/session ownership, coordinated with Reload/close. Retain single-save edits and revision updates; an obsolete result must not regress the current revision or overwrite recovery storage. Alternatively serialize permitted Save/Reload transactions without blocking text edits.
findings.test: Actual panel+main deferred-import regression with refresh callbacks completed in reverse order; normal typing while one Save is pending; reload/new-edit ownership; close/reopen recovery.

findings.title: Artwork coverage audit demands files for locales intentionally excluded by a template
findings.trigger: A valid template declares languages:["en"] in an en/zh catalog. The compiler deliberately produces only en and runtime preserves the original for zh.
findings.observed: The coverage audit iterates all catalog languages, reports generated/zh/title.png missing, and exits 1. Both Catalog.structure and actual compiler prepare accept the same catalog. Existing shipped templates target both locales, so this is a valid authoring-configuration false failure rather than a current gameplay failure.
findings.minimalFix: Build required generated paths from template.languages when present, otherwise all catalog locales, matching compiler/renderer/runtime. Continue flagging missing outputs for included locales.
findings.test: Valid excluded locale passes with only included output; missing included output fails; omitted languages retains all-locale audit.

findings.title: A retired UI load can cancel the next screen transition and its callback
findings.trigger: Cancel an opening while the prefab is pending, start a new transition, then receive successful completion for the retired prefab.
findings.evidence: Actual UIMgr.openUIWithOwner/UIMgr.open→ResourceMgr→UITouch.onShowTransition/cancelTransition. Both control and late cases retire the original request exactly once and instantiate zero stale nodes. The control delivers the next transition callback once. Late success instead stops the newer tween, removes its transition input claim, and delivers zero callbacks.
findings.reachability: Shared opt-in opening contract used by branch purchases and legacy entry. New battle start/arrival transitions have gameplay continuations that open the battle or clear pause. This probe proves suppression of the newer continuation, without claiming that a player encountered it in prior live tests.
findings.minimalFix: Settle a retired owner without affecting the global transition. Scope transition cancellation to the request that actually owns it, including invalid-parent and recovery-cancel paths. Add old-success/new-transition and old-recovery/new-transition controls.

findings.title: A duplicate queued owned popup is dropped without notifying its owner
findings.trigger: With a popup active, request two owned popups for the same other UID, then close the active popup and finish the queue.
findings.evidence: Actual UIMgr pop queue keeps the first request, drops the second request before dispatch, opens the first once, and drains completely. The second handle still reports finished=false, onOpened=0, onCancel=0. Its caller cannot distinguish pending from discarded.
findings.reachability: Supported owned-open/duplicate popup framework case. Current branch and legacy callers normally prevent their own repeat entry. No assertion that the authored player flow issues duplicate independent requests in ordinary play.
findings.minimalFix: When duplicate suppression deliberately declines an owned request, cancel only the declined request once. Preserve the retained request and ordinary unowned popup behavior.

findings.title: An unlock-listener exception on prefab failure strands the opening queue before recovery
findings.trigger: An in-flight owned prefab fails, and a synchronous blocktouch release subscriber throws while another screen is queued.
findings.evidence: Actual UIMgr/ResourceMgr/UITouch. The input claim is physically released and the listener error remains visible, but isopening stays true, the waiting queue retains one request, only the original load was sent, no recovery prompt is created, and the failed owner remains unfinished. Explicit owner.cancel already has a tested finally block. The separate asynchronous prefab onError branch calls releaseInput before finish(false) without that protection.
findings.reachability: Fault containment at a documented synchronous event-listener boundary. Requires a prefab failure plus a throwing subscriber. Not a normal successful open failure.
findings.minimalFix: Finalize manager and request ownership in a finally path even when input release throws. Preserve the original observable listener error while ensuring either retry/cancel remains available or the abandoned owner is cancelled and queued work proceeds.

findings.title: Applying an untouched image binding or layout writes implicit defaults on Save
findings.trigger: Render a valid record into the editor, click Apply without changing fields, then click Save tables.
findings.evidence: Actual panel _renderImage/_applyImage plus main _backupAndSave changed bytes and created a backup solely to add mode="replace". The fixture uses an authored shipped binding. All 39 shipped image bindings omit mode. A valid older layout with no nodeStyles/nodePathStyles similarly gains two empty top-level objects. Direct Save without Apply correctly reports noChanges. Unknown data is retained in these probes but the authorized zero-edit Save no-write contract is violated.
findings.proof: panel-apply-probe.cjs and panel-apply-results.json. Catalog writes were restricted to isolated ignored fixture directories.
findings.reachability: Normal authoring action on current shipped image data and supported legacy layout data. The runtime treats omitted image mode as replace. This concerns persisted catalog bytes and unnecessary backups/recompilation, not visual styling.
findings.minimalFix: Stage only fields whose displayed values changed, preserving absent optional properties/sections, existing unknown fields and explicit empty values. Compare to the current draft before dirtying it. Test zero field edits through Apply→Save, a real changed field, and explicit legacy defaults.

findings.title: Fresh battle entry persists stamina debit and stage selection before prerequisites for a playable map succeed
findings.trigger: From 100 stamina/stage 1, select fresh stage 2 and start battle. Fail UIGame prefab load then select Cancel, or fail its required map prefab then choose Reload.
findings.observed: All four failed pre-open boundaries leave 95 stamina and selected stage 2 despite no battle, no resumable checkpoint and home still visible. Fresh map failure after the UI prefab opens also leaves 95/no checkpoint on cold relaunch. Normal success and retry-success each charge 5 exactly once.
findings.controls: Actual HomeBattle entry, UITouch transition/clear, UIMgr open/failure path, ResourceMgr load/recovery/resolve and UserData/CacheUtils writes under in-memory storage. Init exception, invalidated parent and interrupted transition are injected lifecycle controls. Actual UIGame.start/BaseUI.loadPrefab exercised for map-failure stage with inert map/controller/node methods. No real SDK/renderer/save.
findings.fix: Capture the intended stage and require the current entry owner throughout. Verify readiness/affordability before starting, then commit debit/stage exactly once when the map can actually be played, or use an equivalent durable admission record that makes the purchased entry resumable across reload. Avoid debiting/re-crediting stale live balances from multiple callbacks. Retain current no-cost checkpoint continuation and single charge on successful retry.
findings.regression: Cover cancellation, stale callbacks, initialization failure, mandatory map retry/reload, resource retries and storage refusal/changed eligibility at commit. Assert stage, stamina, recovery timestamp and resumed checkpoint as well as visibility.

findings.title: Reading a completed final campaign mission synchronously rewrites the unchanged mission record
findings.trigger: Claim authored final task 101 (100 talent unlocks, 100 authored talent levels with 140 rows), then home display, enemy deaths, construction or a treasure draw calls getTaskInfo.
findings.observed: 100 getter calls caused 100 actual CacheUtils writes although all mission values remained at completed task 101. Real preceding task 100 advances to 101 with one write. At endgame this adds redundant full-record serialization/storage on each lethal hit on top of genuine progression writes.
findings.fix: Only save doUpTask when an authored next row exists and the task actually changes. Keep the completed terminal record and all normal transitions.
findings.regression: Repeated reads of a claimed last task write zero times; preceding task advances/saves once.

findings.title: Cancelling the new-feature popup leaves home tutorials disabled after an unlock
findings.trigger: Reach stage 1 wave 5 (first authored optional feature unlock). UINewModular prefab load fails; choose Cancel in the recovery prompt.
findings.observed: initViewTogg marks the announcement as seen and sets canGuide=false before the popup opens. Cancellation produces no CloseUI event. Re-evaluating the home state finds no new unlock, leaves canGuide false, and cannot re-open the omitted notification. startGuide checks canGuide. This lasts for the current home instance until another qualifying unrelated close/reload.
findings.fix: Bind the guide pause and seen-announcement changes to an owned popup request. A canceled/retired request must release this home instance’s guide gate. Mark the announcement as seen on a successful open, or explicitly handle the cancellation under the intended skip policy. Keep the actual unlocked feature accessible.
findings.regression: Actual open and Cancel followed by same-home refresh, plus retry-success and normal close. Assert guide resumes once and previously acknowledged features remain acknowledged.

findings.title: Four game-data editor tests retain temporary projects after successful runs
findings.trigger: Run the ordinary editor test suite repeatedly.
findings.observed: A controlled-temp run of store.test.js passed but left 18 directories / 93 files / 9027 bytes. Static source confirms asset-validation makes an orphan sample image project; integration-save and map-assets each copy A/B/D configs, 629242-byte catalog and 587930-byte Map01 (1901382 input bytes/project) plus generated backups with no teardown. Each successful broad run creates new directories.
findings.fix: Remove only folders created by the current test invocation at its teardown (also on failure), using the verified owned-temp pattern already present in main-save/testing-session. Preserve intentionally retained fixtures and unrelated OS temp contents.
findings.regression: Run under a private empty temp directory, require empty private directory after successful completion and an injected failure. Keep byte-preservation assertions.

findings.title: An unavailable character part texture is requested on every frame until it succeeds
findings.trigger: A real assigned appearance is in use and a part texture load fails or remains unavailable.
findings.observed: The per-image job is deleted immediately in its error callback. The following lateUpdate submits it again. Actual shipped royal-guard assignment, 30 allies, one failed helmet, one available weapon and 60 simulation frames produced 60 helmet requests, 1 weapon request and 1 catalog request. The problem is conditional on a texture failure. No connection to the reported navigation lag is asserted.
findings.fix: Use bounded per-image retry timing while retaining shared in-flight and successful jobs. Allow recovery after the delay and preserve original actor appearance until all required textures exist.
findings.regression: Multiple actors share one failing request at a time; repeated frames within the retry interval start none; a later success applies the authored look and does not reload healthy siblings.

findings.title: Cancel can abandon a required battle continuation after its prefab fails
excluded: Current isMapShopOpen() is false; commerce calls the SDK directly with success/failure cleanup. Its five dialog branches are dormant.

Build atlas does not acquire gameplay pause. GAD optional exit/pause dialog retains its original tappable pause overlay. Optional tutorial load Cancel already releases its owned input without advancing guide data.
Home-page authored stamina charge and failed battle-entry opening are separately assigned to the home/persistence reviewer.
findings.trigger: Take a normal wave/settlement/optional pause path, fail the dialog prefab load, then choose Cancel in resource recovery.
findings.impact: Director resumes and the recovery prompt is gone, but the real callers remain paused or terminal without a continuation. Confirmed 4 current and 2 legacy paths. Failed optional Pause can be reopened manually; mandatory perk/result paths have no ordinary forward action.
findings.checkpoint: UIGame writes the next checkpoint only after the player successfully selects perks and GameCtrl.endRoundGame advances the round. Final reward computation and beginSettlement occur only in UIGameEnd.start. Before that, a full reload would restore the earlier checkpoint (or fresh entry) and replay the wave. Cancel must not skip the perk, silently grant/forfeit settlement, or substitute a destructive reload.
findings.minimalFix: Use an owned required-dialog open for mandatory continuations. Keep a visible actionable Retry recovery for the same live owner until it succeeds. Programmatic Cancel cannot discard a required continuation; internal owner teardown may cancel and release the owned request. Optional Pause failure/cancel releases only its own pause. Keep actual round/settlement processing at the original successful callback/start boundary.
testPlan: Failed mandatory prefab keeps actionable recovery across repeated Cancel; late original callback is inert. Retry loads one dialog, and one user decision advances/settles once.
Destroy/restart/replace owner while waiting or retrying releases its pause/input and cannot open a stale choice or mutate a new battle.
Optional Pause cancel returns to prior gameplay/other pause ownership; successful Pause exit and manual resume retain current semantics.
Exercise all current mandatory UIBuff/result/retry calls and both legacy GAD lottery/result paths.

findings.title: Early recipient death drains the shaman healing-effect pool
findings.trigger: Shaman 90009 executes its normal healing cast and the recipient dies before the attached Spine clip completes. Shipped chapter 2 wave 5 can spawn this unit.
findings.evidence: Actual 90009 config/doAttack, GameEffect.onBuff, Interface.delAllBuff, PoolMgr and Creator 2.4.13 NodePool/removeAllChildren. 32 ordinary casts reused one effect and left 11 nodes available. With early recipient teardown all 32 effects were different and detached, none returned/destroyed, zero available, and 33 instantiations occurred versus 12 in the control.
findings.impact: Loss of reusable effect instances and repeated allocation under combat. No inference about retained JS heap size. The previously recorded late aura was visual-only until this pool-ownership consequence was demonstrated.
findings.minimalFix: Own each checked-out healing effect by recipient generation and release it exactly once on animation completion or recipient teardown. A late cold-load callback targeting a recycled/destroyed recipient immediately returns its effect. Preserve healing amount, animation, and timing.
testPlan: Warm pool, concurrent heals, recipient death/reuse before success/completion, repeated callbacks and normal animation completion keep pool bounded without double return or stale attachment.

findings.title: Route-end Wait recovery starts the transforming boss moving before its new form appears
findings.trigger: 90010 changes to 90011 (or 90011 to 90012) with a live opponent within search distance but outside attack range.
findings.evidence: The shipped 0.6667s boss transformation explicitly sets Wait and zero velocity, hides the new body, and resumes Move in spAniUp completion. Eight actual boss onUpdate calls over 0.1333s moved the unit 13.88px with the transform active and the new form hidden. The probe uses shipped configuration and actual getFind/getSpeed/getAttSpeed.
findings.impact: A boss advances during its authored transformation hold. Ordinary route-exhausted enemies still need the earlier Wait reacquisition fix.
findings.minimalFix: Guard only a current transforming boss from movement/attacks until its owned transform completes. Reset transform ownership on pool reuse/death/restart, account for pause, and retain normal Wait target reacquisition.
testPlan: Current transformation holds position before clip completion with in-range and chase targets, then resumes ordinary AI. Reuse/death/stale callback does not resume the wrong lifetime. Ordinary nontransforming Wait enemies still reacquire targets.

findings.title: Failed managed-preview starts and extension unload can leave owned test windows unclosed
findings.reachability: Developer-managed Testing start and extension unload. Conditional native BrowserWindow/webContents failures; not ordinary gameplay or evidence of the reported desktop-control symptom.
evidence: Actual shutdown with first setAudioMuted throwing leaves both owned windows alive and prevents the second cleanup. Ordinary two-window control destroys both.
Actual start with setAudioMuted or loadURL synchronous failure creates a window but neither destroys nor records it; a later shutdown cannot reach it.
A rejected promise-form loadURL is unhandled and start reports generic loading timeout instead of the actual refusal.
findings.minimalFix: Capture window ownership before fallible startup, retain it when destruction fails, consume promise-form navigation failures and preserve mute-before-load. Unload must attempt every captured owned window despite one mute/destroy failure, preserve replacements, and surface cleanup errors after remaining attempts.
validationPlan: No URL starts if muting fails; failed setup closes or keeps an addressable owned window.
Async navigation rejection is handled and reported promptly with no unhandled promise.
Shutdown mute errors do not prevent destroy; a failed destroy retains only that owner while others close; replacement ownership survives.
Normal start/close/reset/status remain compatible with old callback and newer promise forms.

findings.title: Destroyed equipment panels remain subscribed while the item catalog is unavailable
findings.trigger: A hero-items catalog request fails or remains pending. Open Equipment and switch to another home tab repeatedly before the catalog becomes ready.
findings.proof: item-ready-lifetime.cjs and item-ready-lifetime-results.json. Actual UIHome.showView destroys old panels, actual HomePersonCtrl.start registers fresh callbacks, actual inherited BaseCtrl.onDestroy runs, actual HeroItemLooks loader retains/delivers them. Only engine nodes/asset delivery/visual layout were inert.
findings.observed: 30 destroyed equipment panels left30 callbacks in the module-level listeners array after one failed request. One successful retry visited all30 retired owner nodes before refreshing the one live panel. The list cleared only at successful recovery. Repeated tab visits under a persistent failure retain one closure/controller per visit.
findings.impact: Conditional retained scene/controller references and unnecessary fan-out on recovery. cc.isValid already prevents stale drawing. No incorrect currency/award, measured FPS or literal heap-size claim.
findings.minimalFix: Return an idempotent unsubscription from HeroItemLooks.whenReady, retain it on the equipment component, and release it when that component is destroyed before normal BaseCtrl cleanup. Keep shared loading/retry and the current panel callback.
findings.regression: Reproduce multiple tab lifetimes across failure/backoff; destruction removes only that panel subscription, the currently live panel still refreshes once, and already-ready catalogs perform no duplicate work.

findings.title: Concurrent first-use prefab requests repeatedly destroy and rebuild the same warm pool
findings.mechanism: Each caller checks for a pool node before starting an asynchronous load, then unconditionally instantiates a delivery node and calls PoolMgr.creatrePool on completion. The second completion for the same key clears every previously warmed node and its owned template before rebuilding. Every valid checkout is still delivered.
findings.trigger: Multiple requests for the same scoped key arrive before the first prefab callback. A level-one Barracks creates four soldiers in one roster pass. A shaman can request up to ten identical heal effects per attack. Several ItemGood awards/rows or matching wave spawns can also request one key concurrently.
findings.evidence: cold-pool-probe.cjs / cold-pool-results.json execute current GameCtrl.addEnemy/addSoldier, GameEffect.onBuff, PoolMgr and installed Creator 2.4 CCNodePool, with inert nodes and deterministic deferred prefab completions. Compared to identical sequential controls. Four allies allocated 12/destroyed 6 instead of 5/0; four enemies 48/33 instead of 12/0; ten shaman effects 120/99 instead of 12/0. Counts include owned template and retained warm nodes.
findings.classification: Conditional first-use or post-clear allocation/destruction spike. No measured end-to-end FPS attribution and no dropped deliveries in this probe.
exclusions: GAD_UIGameView.onLoad deliberately sets new scene-owned templates for two distinct named pools. Preserve explicit replace behavior in PoolMgr.creatrePool.
ResourceMgr.getNode already performs post-load checkHasPool before setup and does not replace the pool on simultaneous callbacks.
findings.minimalFix: Recheck and acquire the current pool at completion for same-key checkout requests, priming it only once and preserving the first request delivery, existing warm capacities, owner/generation checks, pendingEnemySpawns and award counts. A shared acquire-from-loaded-prefab operation can cover all sixteen callbacks while leaving explicit replacement unchanged.
findings.regression: Run actual concurrent and sequential stock/burst cases above. Confirm all unique live nodes, single owned template, warm capacity, zero unnecessary destroys, one actor init/award delivery per request, owner rejection and explicit pool replacement still effective.
keyAndTemplateIdentity: Both actor keys include team-specific prefix and immutable source config ID. Enemy loads i.prefab and ally loads Play + i.prefab from the same Enemy bundle on every request for that team/ID. Concurrent callbacks in the reproduction use the identical loaded prefab object.

The two generic effects each have a fixed EnemyAttack or EnemyDead key and effect prefab. findings.title: Malformed percent escapes in the web query can abort legacy mode entry
findings.trigger: Home subgame 0 entry with a malformed percent escape in a query key ahead of isEditor/isRemote or in the selected flag value. On EDITOR, GAD_App adds its blocker before initial config loading; all platforms evaluate isEditor on legacy UI load.
findings.evidence: legacy-query-probe.cjs / legacy-query-results.json run actual GAD_App.enter_App, GAD_DataMgr.load/getUrlParam and GAD_UIGame.onLoad. EDITOR ?%zz=unused&isEditor=1 throws URIError before any config resource is requested with the blocker still installed. WEB ?isEditor=%ff throws from actual onLoad. Valid first duplicate and literal plus controls retain their existing results. Unrelated malformed values are skipped normally. Web attachment is stubbed; blocker proof is definitive on the earlier EDITOR path.
findings.minimalFix: Safely decode each key and the first matching value, treating malformed flag input as unavailable while continuing past unrelated malformed keys. Preserve first duplicate, literal plus, valid percent-decoded strings and null when absent; avoid introducing URLSearchParams duplicate/plus semantics.
findings.regression: Actual getUrlParam, load and onLoad exercise malformed unrelated and selected input, valid encoded keys/values and legacy first-duplicate/plus conventions.

findings.summary: Localization panel can overwrite or erase the only recoverable unsaved draft after an unchanged authoring action.
findings.trigger: Edit and close, reopen without restoring the offered recovery, then Apply unchanged template, Add existing layout, or import a semantically identical complete CSV. The 500ms draft debounce writes the unchanged on-disk snapshot over the recoverable edits. A direct clean Save also removes that existing recovery, although the normal button starts disabled.
findings.confirmed: draft-recovery-results.json: all 4 catalogs byte-identical, zero file writes/compiles, prior draft text lost on all 4; actual panel/main code on memory-only boundaries.
findings.relatedBranches: Image/layout currently compare JSON.stringify; reordering JSON keys alone marks false dirty while main uses JSONDocument.equal. Use that existing semantic comparator on these authoring paths too.
findings.fix: Use semantic no-op handling for import, apply template/layout/artwork and Add existing layout; do not send a clean Save or discard an unrelated offered recovery. Real edits and owner/epoch safeguards remain intact.
findings.regression: Retain offered recoverable bytes, untouched catalog revision, clean state, zero timer/IPC/disk/artwork on all no-op variants; prove material edits/restore/save still correct.

findings.summary: Importing an unchanged exported translation CSV materializes omitted optional fields and rewrites a previously untouched catalog.
findings.trigger: toCSV exports absent optional context/locale as empty; mergeCSV unconditionally sets each field for every row.
findings.confirmed: Unchanged actual shipped 1,173-entry export/import created five empty context keys and changed revision, triggering backup/write. An independently valid incomplete locale adds both missing fr and context. Explicit empty/intentional clears/unknown metadata controls recorded.
findings.fix: Preserve omitted empty fields on existing rows; retain explicit blanks, nonempty edits, clears, new row semantics, new locale rules, unknown metadata and revision protection.
findings.regression: Roundtrip the shipped catalog, include partial CSV edits/clears, new rows, missing/explicit blanks and prove zero file/import/artwork effects on unchanged Save.
