Tower projectiles can fly straight through a stationary target during supported slow frames and delay damage for seconds
findings.behavior: The common projectile tests only the starting point against its 25px impact radius. At the supported 0.1s simulation step and the actual tower prefab speed 550, shot and target on the same horizontal line at 137.5px, the third step travels from 110 to 165 through the target with zero damage. It then turns behind the target and travels over 460px away before first damage at 2.6s. The same authored shot at 60FPS hits at 0.233s. This is deterministic actual BulletBuild.setTag and BulletBase.onUpdate/onDie; no live FPS assumptions.
findings.fix: Detect intersection of the proposed steered movement segment and the existing impact radius before it crosses and exits that radius in one update. Use existing onDie/shot identity and short-circuit retirement; preserve travel/steering/position and damage timing for previously normal shots reaching the radius on ordinary steps. Do not snap an off-axis shot to a distant target. Include a near miss and already-dead/reused target controls.
findings.excluded: Enemy08 has a distinct straight-line capped movement override. No change to its authored speed or reference timing is required.

findings.title: Self-removing projectiles can skip the adjacent live projectile’s entire simulation tick
findings.behavior: Each of the four active projectile lists uses Array.forEach. A consuming projectile removes itself by splicing its current list when post-impact time runs out or its target is invalid. The next live shot shifts into the visited index and receives no update. In all four actual subclass controls, an adjacent shot already in range registers no hit in the first frame and hits in the second, while the identical shot alone hits in the first frame. This is independent of movement-step overshoot.
findings.fix: Preserve forward update order and ensure each projectile present and still eligible for a tick receives one update or is retired. Avoid copying all active arrays every frame. Include adjacent/simultaneous disposal plus stable no-disposal, and first-frame in-range hit controls for all four.

findings.scope: Localization editor search, no battle-time path
findings.title: Layout search examines the complete node-binding maps once per layout on every keystroke
findings.entry: ready binds search.oninput to _render. In layout mode _render calls _renderLayoutList; opening Layouts also runs it on an empty query.
findings.proof: layout-query-operations.cjs uses current _renderLayoutList, shipped catalog, inert DOM and read-only property proxies. 338 layouts × (545 node bindings + 320 path bindings) yields 292,370 binding reads, 676 complete map enumerations per search even with no search text, versus 0 or 865 reads plus 0 or 2 enumerations for an equivalent per-render reverse index. Eight blank, matching, missing, and specific ID/path queries yielded identical selected keys in identical order. No permanent caches or invalidation are required.
findings.timing: layout-query.cjs ran eight warm measurements for each of four queries using the current real catalog and current method, with inert DOM nodes. Means were about 66–105 ms here. Concurrent work and device speeds vary; deterministic operation counts establish the regression independently of timing.
findings.mechanism: Within the filter callback for each label style, Object.keys rescans nodeStyles/nodePathStyles and compares every binding value against just that layout. Each keypress and Layouts-tab entry does the same work.
findings.fix: Return sorted layout keys directly on a blank filter. For a nonempty filter, group bound node IDs/path IDs by style in one pass over each map per render. Preserve original key/path iteration order, whitespace and case-insensitive search text, list sorting and current selection. Avoid permanent caches to reflect freshly applied bindings.
findings.regression: Use independent normalized result oracle against the shipped catalog with queries matching keys, text, asset IDs, node paths and nothing. Count binding table reads/enumerations rather than asserting elapsed times. Apply then reassign bindings to prove immediate visibility. No styling or saved-state changes.

findings.title: A failed native reward journal can be published by another save and erase progress earned afterward.
findings.trigger: WeChat or ByteDance native data.json write fails while a gift claim stages its journal, then an unrelated normal save reaches native disk before retryRewardRecovery.
findings.proof: Actual CacheUtils + PlayerMgr claim/recovery + UserData.addGoldNum with memory-only SDK/native file and localStorage boundaries. Eight combinations: two hosts × previous journal tombstone/never existed × mirror also failed/succeeded. In all, 123-gold claim returns null and initial file keeps old/no journal, independent +17 fully saved, unrelated whole-file serialization publishes rejected journal. Retry credits gift, but leaves exactly 123 gold instead of retaining independent 17 (140 with gift, or 17 if the rejected claim never commits).
findings.firstWriteRisk: No preexisting authoritative journal and mirror write succeeds: even reloading the unmodified authoritative SDK file still reads the rejected journal via mirror fallback. Seen on both hosts. A pointer-only mutation rollback is insufficient.
findings.cause: CacheUtils.saveData mutates wx/tt.sffile in place before native write and writes the new mirror even on authoritative failure. getData reads the in-memory native dictionary first, then the mirror on missing keys.
findings.minimalFix: Stage complete candidate native dictionary, serialize/write first, and publish the new in-memory value and mirror only after authoritative success. Leave both previous copies intact on native failure. Keep web-only flow and native success despite mirror quota errors. Replace obsolete assertion that explicitly permitted the rejected native write to change its mirror. Verify existing/absent journal, both hosts, tail retry+next legitimate claim and exact unrelated-progress retention.
findings.limits: Simulated native SDK storage, no live mini-app release. A specific reproducible cross-boundary failure; not a claim every native save loses progress.

findings.title: A rejected Add artwork creates an optional section in a sparse draft that later persists on an unrelated save
findings.reachability: Editor-only. Valid v1 catalogs may omit images. The shipped catalog already has the section.
findings.trigger: Use a valid binding identifier and an as-yet unknown translation key in an otherwise valid sparse v1 catalog. Add binding correctly reports that the translation must be created first. Make and save an unrelated translation edit afterwards.
findings.proof: optional-image.cjs with actual panel+main methods / optional-image-results.json. No writes occur on the immediate error and the panel stays clean, but images:{} is added to the live catalog and lands in a later explicit unrelated Save. Identical control preserves absence. draft-rejections.cjs / draft-rejections.json check seven other error paths stay byte-equivalent at the catalog-object level.
findings.fix: Look up the optional images table without assigning it while validating. Only create/attach that table after both duplicate-ID and existing-translation-key checks succeed. Preserve normal first-image creation, rendered row, and one dirty event. Regression should verify rejected first binding leaves the draft and subsequent unrelated save without an images field.

findings.title: FormatDate1 combines a local year with a UTC month/day at New Year
findings.reachability: Exported date utility with no current use found in game, editor or tool code. No player progression or displayed-date claim.
findings.trigger: Format a timestamp crossing December 31 / January 1 between UTC and the local time zone.
findings.proof: date-boundary.cjs runs the actual exported function in isolated Node processes with scoped TZ. In Europe/Paris, 2025-12-31T23:30Z yields 2026/12/31. findings.fix: Use getUTCFullYear to match the two established UTC fields, preserving unpadded numbers, default and custom separators. Verify both offset directions and same-year controls.
